page.meta_desc: content="Learn Conquer, the 1987 Usenet strategy game, one key at a time: a recorded first turn with every screen, from signing in to the turn update."
page.og_desc: content="The 1987 Usenet strategy game, back in your browser. Learn it one key at a time."
page.lede: A real first turn of a new nation, key by key: sign in, read the reports, march out to take land, draft troops, and hand in your orders. Every screen below comes from the game itself.
page.player_note: The recording above is the real terminal: pause it at any moment, and select and copy its text.
page.l_reverse: <dt>reverse</dt><dd>letters shown in reverse video are sectors you own</dd>
page.l_star: <dd>in the unit list: the selected unit</dd>
page.map_d: Press <kbd>d</kbd> in the game to switch the map to vegetation, people, food and more.
page.h_rules: Four rules that save your first year
page.r1: Big enough to conquer. An army takes empty land only with at least 75 soldiers and one for every 350 of your people. Send your largest field army.
page.r2: Drafting stops an army. Troops added to an army use up its movement for the turn. Raise them as a new army.
page.r3: Food first. A capital alone grows no food. Take flat land with good vegetation and turn it into farms (r on a sector you own).
page.r4: Quit when you are done. The turn cannot run while you are in the game. Press q and mark your orders done.
page.p_practice: Option 7 in the game menu opens your own practice world: the same game, with nobody else in it. Try anything, run the next turn yourself and start again whenever you like. The coach (Coach button above the game) walks you through this same turn inside the terminal.
page.cta_try: >Or try it in your browser, no account needed
